items.title: Cohort 7 opens with twelve world builders
items.body: Twelve teams join the autumn speedrun, from a floating bazaar in Aria to a night ferry that links three club cities.

items.title: Satin Swans close a 1.2M SUM community round
items.body: The club sold out its first round in four hours. Members voted to spend half on a new runway hall in Brocade.

items.title: Reward weights move toward hosting
items.body: Hosting a meetup now earns more SUM than flipping a PFT, after a Phidao vote passed with 71 percent.

items.title: September rewards paid
items.body: $SUM rewards for logged functions were distributed to 18,240 members.

items.title: Demo day returns to the Atelier Nine dome
items.body: Nine teams pitch live to members on November 14. Every member can back a team with as little as 10 SUM.

items.title: Forty new functions join the registry
items.body: Quest scoring, ride booking and look fitting are now logged functions with their own rewards.

items.title: How the Velvet Pack paid for its own city
items.body: A club of ninety members turned weekly runway nights into a treasury large enough to fund a district.

items.title: Autumn cohort funded
items.body: Nine clubs receive $SUM support alongside their Phipad funding.

items.title: Lantern Row raises for a market street
items.body: The market team wants stalls that change with the season. Their round closes on October 30.

items.title: Quarterly report: inflows up 18 percent
items.body: Most new SUM came from ride fees and hosted events. Spending stayed inside the budget the DAO set.

items.title: Mentors announced for the speedrun
items.body: Builders from Phipad, Phiora and four founding clubs will hold weekly office hours.

items.title: New functions registered
items.body: Fitting and runway-seat functions are now in the registry.

items.q: Can I back a cohort team?
items.a: Yes. Open the team on demo day and pledge any amount of SUM from your wallet.
At the start of each month, for every function logged in the month before.
The cohort team scores each project, then members vote on the shortlist.
Clubs apply the same way as teams. The club treasury signs the application.
